name: kiln-and-cup

subject.name: Kiln & Cup
subject.audience: Buyers of handmade tableware choosing a one-of-a-kind piece online, from photographs alone
subject.primaryJob: Let a buyer trust how a single wood-fired piece will feel in the hand, then buy it without pressure
sources: Wood-fired stoneware: natural ash glaze, flashing where the flame passed, iron-speckled clay bodies
The thrown rim: a continuous curve made on the wheel, never drafted
The studio after a firing: cooling kiln, ash on the shelves, pieces set out on wooden boards

principles: Beauty in everyday objects meant to be used
Natural materials and honest making, shown rather than styled
Variation from the fire is part of each piece, not a flaw
Quiet surfaces that let the work lead

territories.name: The workshop after a firing
territories.description: The studio the morning the kiln is opened: still-warm ware set out on oiled boards, ash dust on the shelves, low light from a high window across glaze and bare clay.
territories.light: warm, low and directional, through a high window, catching glaze runs
territories.textures: glaze pooling, toasted clay, wood grain under the pots; never applied as a filter
territories.composition: one piece at a time, generous margin, the photograph leads
territories.type: plain humanist text, a calm book serif for names of pieces
territories.motion: slow and settled, like a piece set down on a board
territories.imagery: honest daylight photographs of a piece held, in use, and on the board, with its marks shown

muse.name: Lucie Rie
muse.take: Economy and poise: thin, confident walls and rims, restraint that lets the glaze carry the piece
muse.leave: Her specific forms, sgraffito lines and glaze recipes; the studio's ware is its own

samples.action: Add this cup to your basket
samples.confirmation: It's yours. We'll wrap it and send it this week.
samples.error: That piece has just gone to someone else. Each one is single, so we can't make another the same.

signature.reason: Every corner takes the continuous, never-drafted curve of a rim pulled on the wheel; squircle corners carry that curve where a circular arc would show a seam.

avoid: Brush lettering or Japanese calligraphic display type
Indigo and kraft paper as a borrowed Japanese look
Countdown timers, scarcity banners or any hard sell

rationale.form.corner: The signature: the rim's continuous curvature, which only the squircle corner holds without a visible join.
rationale.form.curvature: Round rather than the canon's soft: a rim reads as a full, generous curve, not a nicked edge; still short of pill, which would read as a product sticker.
rationale.iconography.set: Phosphor at light weight matches the workshop's hairline line and stays quiet next to photographs.
rationale.grounding.primary: Reinterpret: take mingei's values (use, honest material, variation from making) and leave its look: no brush lettering, no indigo and kraft; the studio is not a Japanese brand.
rationale.color.anchors.0: Natural ash glaze, the green the wood ash leaves on the shoulder of a pot; a dark solid for the main role.
rationale.color.anchors.2: The flashing where flame crosses bare clay; kept toward ochre so it never reads as terracotta.
